brief:
The Human Rights Foundation announced funding for seven Bitcoin initiatives aimed at people living under authoritarian regimes, according to Bitcoin Magazine. The projects, supported through HRF's Bitcoin Development Fund, focus on self-custody, privacy and education tools adapted for conditions of repression. The initiatives range from mobile phone wallets to solar-powered mining operations.

The fund targets technological gaps that limit Bitcoin access in countries with restrictive governance. Projects address both practical barriers—such as limited electricity infrastructure—and security concerns facing users in surveillance-prone environments.
